documents.title: H&P - Admission - Septic Shock, Urinary Source
lines: ADMISSION H&P
HD1, note written 06:20
CC: confusion, fever, weakness x1 day
HPI:
91 yo male brought in by daughter at 02:10 for acute confusion and fever.
Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
Daughter notes decreased PO intake x2 days, malodorous urine, one episode of incontinence.
No cough, no sputum, no chest pain, no diarrhea, no rash, no recent fall.
No recent hospitalization. No indwelling catheter. No known urinary retention.
Last antibiotic exposure unknown, none in recent months per daughter.
PMH:
HTN, paroxysmal AF on low dose apixaban, BPH, CKD stage 2 (baseline Cr 0.9), osteoarthritis.
Remote TURP. Cholecystectomy.
Home meds: apixaban 2.5 mg BID, metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qHS, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: sulfa (rash).
Social: lives alone in one story home, daughter visits daily, uses cane outdoors. No tobacco, rare alcohol.
ROS: positive for fever, chills, generalized weakness, confusion. Negative for dyspnea at rest per daughter, no vomiting.
ED COURSE:
Temperature 37.9 C at triage; WBC 11,200.
Triage HR 104, BP 96/54, RR 24.
Respiratory rate 30; SpO2 88% on RA, placed on 6L NC with SpO2 93%.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30. Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Norepinephrine discussed by ED team for MAP 64; held after additional fluid with MAP 68.

Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics; blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Vitals at 06:00: T 38.4 C, HR 110, BP 94/56, RR 24, SpO2 94% on 4L NC.
Gen: frail elderly male, ill appearing, warm and diaphoretic.
Neuro: awake, oriented to self only, follows simple commands, no focal deficit, no neck stiffness.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no scleral icterus.
CV: tachycardic, irregularly irregular, no murmur, JVP flat.
Pulm: tachypneic, clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheeze.
Abd: soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no CVA tenderness, no rebound, bladder not distended.
GU: no scrotal swelling, no penile discharge.
Ext: warm, cap refill 3 sec, no edema. Skin intact, no cellulitis.
LABS:
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Na 133, K 4.4, HCO3 19, BUN 42, glucose 146, AG 17.
AST 30, ALT 24, T bili 1.1, alb 3.0, INR 1.3.
Trop 22 ng/L, flat on repeat. VBG pH 7.31, pCO2 32.
CXR: low lung volumes, no consolidation or effusion.
EKG: AF at 112, no ischemic changes.
ASSESSMENT:
91 yo male with sepsis, likely urinary source, with fluid responsive hypotension, AKI and thrombocytopenia.
Sepsis physiology with hyperlactatemia and encephalopathy. Vasopressors deferred after further fluid.
PLAN:
1. Sepsis: continue IV pip-tazo and vancomycin, follow culture and sensitivities, deescalate when available.
2. Hemodynamics: MAP goal >65, additional 500 mL NS boluses prn, low threshold to start pressors, q1h vitals.
3. Repeat lactate q6h until clearing. Monitor UOP, Foley placed for strict I/O.
4. AKI: hold amlodipine, avoid NSAIDs, trend BMP BID, renally dose meds.
5. Thrombocytopenia: hold apixaban, daily CBC, no heparin gtt.
6. Respiratory: wean O2 to keep SpO2 >92%.
7. Delirium: reorientation, sleep protocol, avoid benzodiazepines, daughter at bedside during day.
8. Continue metoprolol at reduced dose if BP tolerates. Telemetry for AF.
9. PT/OT when stable. Code status: full per patient and daughter, will revisit.
Discussed with daughter at bedside 06:15. Admit to step down unit.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning - Sepsis, Urinary Source
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:40
S: Pt more interactive overnight, now oriented to self and place. Denies pain. Ate half of breakfast.
Overnight: two 500 mL NS boluses for MAP 62. No pressors required. UOP 620 mL over 12 h.
O: T 37.6 C, HR 92, BP 108/62, MAP 77, RR 20, SpO2 95% on 2L NC.
I/O: in 3.1 L, out 780 mL since admission.
Gen: less toxic appearing. Neuro: attentive to questions, no asterixis.
CV: irregular, rate controlled. Pulm: clear, no increased work of breathing.
Abd: soft, suprapubic tenderness improved. Ext: warm, trace pedal edema.
Foley draining clear yellow urine.
Labs 05:00: WBC 9,800, Hgb 11.4, platelets 96,000, Cr 1.9, K 4.0, HCO3 21.
Lactate 1.8 this morning, down from repeat value.

Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics; blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours.
Urine culture pending, gram negative rods on prelim smear.
A: Sepsis with urinary source, improving. Fluid responsive hypotension resolved. AKI improving. Thrombocytopenia improving.
P:
1. Continue pip-tazo and vancomycin pending sensitivities.
2. Maintenance IVF NS at 75 mL/h, reassess this afternoon.
3. Trend lactate, BMP, CBC.
4. Wean O2 as tolerated, off NC if SpO2 >92% on RA.
5. Hold apixaban while platelets <100,000.
6. Foley out when MAP stable off boluses and pt mobilizing.
7. PT eval today, up with assist.
8. Updated daughter by phone 07:35.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon - Interval Reassessment
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 15:30 interval note
S: Pt sitting up in chair, oriented to self, place and month. Reports feeling much better. Walked 15 feet with PT and walker.
No fever since 09:00. No dyspnea. Tolerating regular diet.
O: 15:00 vitals: T 37.1 C, HR 84, BP 116/68, MAP 84, RR 18, SpO2 94% on room air, off NC since 13:20.
UOP 340 mL since 07:00, clear.
Exam: alert, conversant. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Extremities warm, cap refill <2 sec.
Repeat lactate 1.3 at 14:00.
Micro update: blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours, sensitivities pending.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
Vancomycin trough drawn pre 4th dose, pending.
A: E. coli bacteremia from urinary source, clinically improved. Off supplemental O2. Hemodynamically stable without vasopressors.
AKI resolving, Cr trending down. Thrombocytopenia improving.
P:
1. Continue pip-tazo; plan to stop vancomycin once no gram positives on final blood culture.
2. Reduce IVF to NS 50 mL/h, discontinue in AM if PO intake adequate.
3. Foley discontinued at 15:20, monitor for retention, bladder scan q6h x2.
4. Repeat BMP and CBC in AM.
5. Resume amlodipine only if BP remains >120 systolic.
6. Continue delirium precautions, mobilize with PT BID.
7. Anticipate transfer out of step down tonight if vitals remain stable.
8. Daughter updated at bedside 15:25, asked about home antibiotic plan; discussed.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - E. coli Bacteremia and UTI
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted HD1, discharged HD3. LOS 3 days.
Discharge diagnoses: 1. Sepsis due to E. coli urinary tract infection with bacteremia. 2. AKI on CKD. 3. Thrombocytopenia, resolving. 4. Toxic metabolic encephalopathy. 5. Paroxysmal AF.
BRIEF COURSE:
91 yo male presented at 02:10 with fever and acute confusion.
Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
Temperature 37.9 C at triage; WBC 11,200.
Respiratory rate 30; SpO2 88% on RA, placed on 6L NC with SpO2 93%.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30. Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Norepinephrine discussed by ED team for MAP 64; held after additional fluid with MAP 68.

Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics; blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Pt was fluid responsive and never required vasopressors. Lactate cleared to 1.3 by HD2 afternoon. Weaned to room air HD2 13:20.
Urine culture grew E. coli >100,000 CFU/mL, pansensitive including ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin. Vancomycin stopped HD3 after no gram positive growth.
Mentation returned to baseline by HD3, oriented x3, recognized daughter, following conversation normally.
Foley removed HD2, voided spontaneously, post void residual 40 mL.
DISCHARGE LABS HD3: WBC 7,600, Hgb 11.1, platelets 142,000, Cr 1.2, K 4.1, HCO3 24, lactate 1.0.
Discharge vitals: T 36.8 C, HR 78, BP 122/70, RR 16, SpO2 96% RA. Ambulating with walker, PT cleared for home with daughter.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID x4 more days to complete therapy for bacteremic UTI.
Apixaban 2.5 mg PO BID, resumed HD3 after platelet recovery.
Metoprolol succinate 25 mg PO daily.
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO qHS.
Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily - HELD, do not resume until BP rechecked.
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h prn.
FOLLOW UP:
Primary care in 3 to 5 days for BMP, CBC and BP check; discuss resuming amlodipine.
Return for fever >38.0 C, confusion, dysuria, inability to urinate, lightheadedness, bleeding or unusual bruising.
Encourage oral fluids 6 to 8 glasses daily. Daughter will stay with pt for first week.
Home PT ordered for gait and strength.
Discharge instructions reviewed with pt and daughter at bedside 11:40; both verbalized understanding.
Condition at discharge: stable, improved.
